decisions.reason: As a generic utility only loosely tied to the firm's differentiated energy-regulation platform, it likely fell below aspiration levels versus core offerings and its resources are better redeployed.

Although close to the firm's database business, the Austrian gas-grid niche is likely too small and uncertain to justify continued attention if it did not quickly match aspirations set by stronger domestic products.
This service fits the firm's core analytical and compliance capabilities in regulated energy markets, so with some organizational slack it is worth retaining as a complementary platform module.
A tariff database is closely aligned with the firm's data-centric platform strategy and can reuse existing databases and expertise, making it a product management would likely continue.

Custom web services are less scalable and less consistent with the firm's shift toward standardized SaaS and modular products, so any performance shortfall would trigger reallocation to the core platform.
Like other generic lookup tools, this service offers limited differentiation for the firm's target market and is unlikely to meet aspiration levels relative to higher-value core products.
